# Opcode registry

**Generated by `tools/65x02/gen_opcodes_md.py` — do not edit by hand.**
Run `make opcodes` after changing the decode table or the allocation
policy. The implemented set is read from `rtl/cpu6502_decode.sv`, so this
file cannot claim an instruction the hardware does not have.

This is the registry gate **G2** of `add-isa-ergonomic-gates` checks
against: every added instruction is registered here, claims no reserved
slot, and no slot is claimed twice. A slice that needs a slot edits the
policy tables in the generator, in the same commit that adds the decode
row.

| | slots |
| --- | --- |
| Implemented | 161 |
| Reserved for 65C02 compatibility | 58 |
| Extension space, claimed | 10 |
| Extension space, assigned but unclaimed | 23 |
| Unallocated | 14 |
| **Total** | **256** |

## Implemented

Cycles are this core's, measured over the full 65x02 sweep and recorded in
`docs/cpu-timing-v2.json` — **not** NMOS's. They differ: this core has no
read-modify-write dummy write, no page-cross penalty and no dummy stack
access, so pulls, pushes, `RTS`, `RTI`, read-modify-writes and taken
branches are all cheaper than the 6502 books say. Gate **G4** compares a
proposed instruction against the sequence it replaces, so it must be
scored against this column.

## Unallocated

Undefined on NMOS, not defined by the 65C02, and not claimed by any
slice. Available, but claiming one needs a policy change here first.

```
  $22 $34 $42 $44 $54 $5C $62 $82 $C2 $D4 $DC $E2 $F4 $FC
```

## What an unallocated slot does

Every slot with no row in `rtl/cpu6502_decode.sv` decodes to `AM_TRAP`.
The core latches the opcode and the address it was fetched from, raises a
sticky `dbg_trap`, and continues as though the byte were a `NOP`. It is
inert on hardware and named in the simulator: a wild jump or a
mis-assembled byte becomes a reported failure instead of silent
corruption. It does not halt — an unrecoverable state is exactly what the
spec forbids.

A slot stops trapping when a slice claims it, which is one row here and
one row in the decode table, in the same commit.
